annotation.title_clean: Robots Should Be Slaves: Perceptions of Bulgarians Towards Potential Robot Rights and Obligations
annotation.title_en: Robots Should Be Slaves: Perceptions of Bulgarians Towards Potential Robot Rights and Obligations
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 397 (Robophilosophy 2024), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper empirically testing Gunkel's robot rights matrix with a survey of 215 Bulgarians across 26 rights and obligations. Respondents viewed robots as incapable of holding rights and as "slaves" with obligations to obey regulations and respect humans; policy and theoretical implications are discussed.
key_provisions_or_claims: Survey of 215 Bulgarian respondents tests Gunkel's robot rights matrix on 26 rights and obligations
Respondents did not think robots/AI can have or should be given rights
Robots seen as slaves without rights to reproduce, own property, strike, salary, vote, but with obligations to obey regulations and respect humans
Respondents did not fully distinguish 'can have' from 'should have'
